parole.significato: A land grant to brahmins for the maintenance of a temple.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Tamil அக்ரஹாரம் (akrahāram), from Sanskrit अग्रहार (agrahāra).

parole.significato: The low-denomination coin of southern India until 1818.
parole.testo: Variant of earlier cass under influence from cash above, from Tamil காசு (kācu), ultimately from Sanskrit karsha ("weight of 1/400 tulā, तुला"). Extended to other similar forms of low-denomination coins in Southeast and East Asia following the example of cognate Portuguese cas, casse, caxa, caixa.

parole.significato: A type of plaster made from lime and sand, used for indoor finishing and slope protection.
parole.testo: From Tamil சுண்ணம் (cuṇṇam, “lime, ground mortar”), from Sanskrit चूर्ण (cūrṇa, “powder; lime”).

parole.significato: A district in India held in feudal tenure by a poligar.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Tamil பாளையம் (pāḷaiyam), from Sanskrit प्लयति (playati, “he guards”), probably akin to Sanskrit पिपर्ति (piparti, “he brings over, rescues”).

parole.testo: Borrowed from Tamil பப்படம் (pappaṭam), from Sanskrit पर्पट (parpaṭa). parole.significato: A spicy South Indian soup made with tamarind juice.
parole.testo: Probably borrowed from Tamil ரசம் (racam), from Sanskrit रस (rasa, “juice”). Doublet of rasa.

parole.significato: A tropical plant of the species Dioscorea alata, cultivated for its edible root.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Tamil இராசவள்ளி (irācavaḷḷi), ultimately from Sanskrit रस (rasa, “juice, essence”) + native Tamil வள்ளி (vaḷḷi, “climber, creeper”).

parole.significato: a trident, a trishula; a sacred weapon used by Hindu deities.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Tamil சூலம் (cūlam), in turn from Sanskrit शूल (śūla) or Sanskrit त्रिशूल (triśūla).
